extraction.name: C-EVAL
extraction.description: C-EVAL is a comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. It comprises 13,948 multiple-choice questions across four difficulty levels (middle school, high school, college, and professional) spanning 52 diverse disciplines across STEM, Social Science, Humanities, and Other areas. It is accompanied by C-EVAL HARD, a subset of 8 challenging subjects requiring advanced reasoning.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He
extraction.citeAs: Huang, Y., Bai, Y., Zhu, Z., Zhang, J., Zhang, J., Su, T., Liu, J., Lv, C., Zhang, Y., Lei, J., Fu, Y., Sun, M., & He, J. (2023). C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models. Thirty-seventh Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023) Track on Datasets and Benchmarks.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from mock exams freely available on the internet, past college exam questions shared by students from top universities in China, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam authorized from the Weipu website. Sourced largely from PDF or Microsoft Word documents rather than structured plain text to mitigate data contamination.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mock exams freely available on the internet, student-shared past college exam questions from top universities in China, and graduate entrance mock exam questions from the Weipu website.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions with fewer than four options were eliminated, and questions with more than four options had incorrect choices randomly dropped so every question has exactly four choices.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents were processed into text. Questions were parsed automatically or manually into structured format. Subjects with complex mathematical notations were manually converted to standard LaTeX format. Standard preprocessing pipelines including deduplication, cleaning, and several rounds of human validation to ensure LaTeX syntax compliance were applied.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions and choices were parsed and structured by the authors. For the development split, explanations were generated by prompting GPT-4 with five human-written question-explanation pairs to generate step-by-step reasoning for the ground-truth answer, followed by manual revision by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human cross-validation was conducted across the collected data by the authors, including manual checks and revisions to ensure valid LaTeX syntax and correct formatting.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The authors of the paper (researchers and students affiliated with Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, and The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The development and validation splits with ground-truth labels are released publicly via GitHub, while test split labels are kept private to prevent contamination. An automated evaluation platform and public leaderboard are maintained at https://cevalbenchmark.com.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to narrow the gap between Chinese large language model development and evaluation, analyze model strengths and shortcomings, and foster model growth for Chinese users across critical domains.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Analysis of option bias showed minor fluctuations in the distribution of correct answers across options A (22.9%), B (26.0%), C (26.4%), and D (24.7%), comparable to MMLU. Option permutation experiments showed relatively small variance across different permutations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: C-EVAL only assesses multi-choice questions and does not cover other model capabilities such as API calling, or aspects beyond accuracy such as safety, bias, and robustness.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Validation and Testing for evaluating advanced knowledge and reasoning capabilities of foundation models and large language models in a Chinese context.
